mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE below 6% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in INDPRO above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals accelerating industrial production, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both UNRATE and PAYEMS below their prior 12-month averages signals a dual deterioration in labor market participation and employment, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both below 12-month averages for the current month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST above 1% from the prior month indicates strengthening housing demand, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary policy and rising inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages for the current month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 3% from the prior month for six consecutive months signals robust retail sales growth, which expands consumer spending and supports higher corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > prior month + 3% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
